answers.question: Explain how I combine Communities and Contexts with Age group to find refugee youth research. Give the exact current all-collection count with Include related research off and on. Explain whether every result directly studies refugee young people.
answers.answer:
The current **all-collection** search for **Refugees & Forced Displacement + Youth & young adults** returns:

- **Include related research off: 12 papers** — direct and contextual coverage. [S1]
- **Include related research on: 25 papers** — adding 13 results through related coverage. [S2]

These are exact visible-library counts from the classification guide updated **30 October 2026**, not counts of full-text availability. [S1][S2]

### How to combine the filters
1. Open **Universal Research → Search papers** and select **All collections**.
2. Under **Communities and Contexts**, select **Refugees & Forced Displacement**.
3. Under **Age group**, select **Youth & young adults**.
4. Toggle **Include related research** to broaden or narrow the results. Different filters combine with **AND**; multiple selections within the same filter use **OR**. [S1]

Open the filtered search directly: [Related off — 12 papers](https://staging.universalmind.tv/informatics/library.html?collection=all&view=search&community=refugees&age=youth) · [Related on — 25 papers](https://staging.universalmind.tv/informatics/library.html?collection=all&view=search&community=refugees&age=youth&related=1).

### Does every result directly study refugee young people?
**No—the filter match does not guarantee that.** With related research off, coverage includes both **direct and contextual** relevance, not exclusively studies recruiting refugee young people. With it on, additional links labelled **Related · inferred** may reflect a shared intervention or outcome rather than refugee participants. They do not establish that findings transfer to refugees. [S1][S2]

Likewise, **Youth & young adults** includes adolescents and source-defined young people. It can indicate a youth-focused study or youth inclusion in a broader sample; it is not a uniform age range or proof of youth-specific effects. Check each publication’s participants, reported ages and study context before describing it as direct evidence about refugee youth. [S1]

answers.question: For domestic and family violence across all ages and all collections, give the direct/contextual count and the total with related research. Are AI-guided recommendations and continuous research already active? Did this feature update fine-tune your model weights?
answers.answer:
For **Domestic & Family Violence**, across **all collections with no age restriction**, the current visible-library counts are:

- **Include related research off: 5 papers** with direct/contextual coverage. [S1]
- **Include related research on: 62 papers total**, adding 57 related results. [S2]

These counts come from the feature guide updated **30 October 2026**. “All ages” here means leaving Age group unfiltered, including records with age not specified—not that every paper studies every age. Related results carry **Related · inferred** links; these do not establish that domestic or family violence participants were studied or that findings transfer to them. [S1][S2]

[Open the direct/contextual search](https://staging.universalmind.tv/informatics/library.html?collection=all&view=search&community=domestic-violence) · [Open the search including related research](https://staging.universalmind.tv/informatics/library.html?collection=all&view=search&community=domestic-violence&related=1)

**Are AI-guided recommendations and continuous research active?**  
No. AI-guided recommendations and the continuous researcher remain **planned features**, with Universal Mind review before publication. The planned approval-triggered knowledge refresh is not an active pipeline. [S1]

**Did this update fine-tune my model weights?**  
No. This is a library classification and discovery update, not model-weight fine-tuning. I retrieve the current guide and counts to answer; that is distinct from training or changing my underlying model.
